title: Adobe AEM reflects a script payload (ContentFinder XSS)
summary: The AEM ContentFinder suggestions endpoint echoes a query parameter into its response without encoding it, so a crafted link runs script in the visitor's session. The check sends a harmless marker and confirms it comes back unencoded.

confirm.control: A path that cannot exist, so the site's not found answer is known and a page that reflects the marker is told apart from it.

reproduce: curl -sk 'https://host/bin/wcm/contentfinder/connector/suggestions.json?query_term=path:/&pre=%3Csvg/onload=alert(1)%3E&post=x' and check the response echoes <svg/onload=alert(1)> unencoded. Unencoded reflection means the parameter is a cross site scripting sink.
remediate: Patch AEM and block the ContentFinder endpoints at the dispatcher if they are not needed. Output encode any reflected value. Follow Adobe's AEM dispatcher security checklist.
